name: Microsoft REST API Guidelines
description: Comprehensive style rules based on Microsoft Azure REST API Guidelines and Microsoft REST API Guidelines. This profile includes ~120 rules covering versioning, URI design, HTTP semantics, error handling, pagination, long-running operations, naming conventions, security, and more.
introduction:
The Microsoft REST API Guidelines are a set of best practices for building consistent, reliable, and user-friendly REST APIs. These guidelines have evolved over many years of API development at Microsoft and represent lessons learned across Azure, Microsoft 365, and other Microsoft services.

This style specification formalizes these guidelines into machine-checkable rules that can be enforced during API design review and validation.

principles.title: Consistency
principles.description: APIs should be consistent with other Microsoft APIs and with common REST conventions. Developers who know one Microsoft API should feel comfortable with others.

principles.title: Simplicity
principles.description: APIs should be simple to understand and use. Avoid unnecessary complexity, and prefer common patterns over custom ones.

principles.title: Predictability
principles.description: API behavior should be predictable. Developers should be able to guess how an API works based on general REST knowledge.

principles.title: Discoverability
principles.description: APIs should be self-documenting and discoverable. Use hypermedia where appropriate to guide clients.

principles.title: Extensibility
principles.description: APIs should be designed to evolve without breaking existing clients. Use versioning and optional fields appropriately.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Overview of Microsoft REST API Guidelines
sections.introduction: These guidelines establish a foundation for API design that promotes consistency across Microsoft services.

patterns.name: Server-Driven Pagination
patterns.summary: Use server-driven pagination with nextLink for large collections
patterns.problem: Collections may contain more items than can be efficiently returned in a single response.
patterns.solution: Return partial results with a nextLink URL pointing to the next page of results.
patterns.when: When returning collections that may contain many items

patterns.name: Long Running Operations
patterns.summary: Use 202 Accepted with Location header for long-running operations
patterns.problem: Some operations take too long to complete within a single HTTP request timeout.
patterns.solution: Return 202 Accepted immediately with a Location header pointing to a status monitor endpoint.
patterns.when: When operations may take more than a few seconds to complete

diagrams.title: LRO Flow
diagrams.content:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    C->>A: POST /resource
    A->>C: 202 Accepted + Location
    loop Until Complete
        C->>A: GET /operations/id
        A->>C: 200 OK (status: running)
    end
    C->>A: GET /operations/id
    A->>C: 200 OK (status: succeeded)

patterns.name: Standard Error Response
patterns.summary: Use consistent error response format with code, message, and details
patterns.problem: Inconsistent error formats make it hard for clients to handle errors programmatically.
patterns.solution: Use a standard error envelope with required code and message fields.

examples.title: Standard Error

patterns.name: Optimistic Concurrency with ETags
patterns.summary: Use ETags and If-Match headers for optimistic concurrency control
patterns.problem: Concurrent updates to the same resource can overwrite each other's changes.
patterns.solution: Return ETags with resources and require If-Match headers on update requests.
patterns.when: When resources can be updated by multiple clients

examples.title: Conditional Update
examples.code:
PATCH /users/123 HTTP/1.1
If-Match: "abc123"
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": "Updated Name"}

glossary.definition: An entity exposed by the API, identified by a URI.
A set of resources of the same type.
An action performed on a resource using an HTTP method.
Long Running Operation - an operation that takes more than a few seconds to complete.
Entity Tag - a version identifier for a resource used in conditional requests.
A URL pointing to the next page of results in a paginated collection.
Open Data Protocol - a standard for building RESTful APIs with query capabilities.
Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State - REST principle where responses include links to related resources.

rules.title: Use api-version query parameter
rules.rationale: Microsoft APIs use the api-version query parameter for versioning. This allows the same URL structure across versions and makes version changes explicit.
rules.description:
All Microsoft REST APIs must include an api-version query parameter in requests. This parameter specifies which version of the API the client wants to use.

The api-version approach was chosen over URI versioning (/v1/...) because:
1. It keeps resource URIs stable across versions
2. It's explicitly visible in every request
3. It works well with API management proxies
rules.background: Microsoft standardized on query parameter versioning after evaluating multiple approaches including URI path versioning and header-based versioning. Query parameter versioning provides the best balance of visibility and URI stability.

detailed.title: Production API Call
detailed.code:
GET /subscriptions/sub-123/resourceGroups?api-version=2024-01-01 HTTP/1.1
Host: management.azure.com
Authorization: Bearer token123

annotations.text: api-version parameter explicitly specifies the version
URI path versioning is not used in Microsoft APIs

judge.prompt: Verify that the API uses api-version query parameter for versioning rather than URI path versioning. Check that api-version is documented as a required parameter.
passCriteria: api-version query parameter is documented or used in examples
No URI path versioning (e.g., /v1/, /v2/) is present
Version format follows Microsoft conventions (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD-preview)
partialCriteria: api-version is present but format may not follow conventions
failCriteria: api-version is not documented or required

rules.title: Version format YYYY-MM-DD
rules.rationale: Microsoft API versions use YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., 2024-01-15) for GA releases and YYYY-MM-DD-preview for preview releases. This format is chronological and unambiguous.
rules.description:
API version strings must follow the YYYY-MM-DD format for general availability releases. Preview versions append '-preview' to the date.

Examples:
- GA: 2024-01-01
- Preview: 2024-06-15-preview

judge.prompt: Check if the API version parameters use YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., 2024-01-15) for GA versions or YYYY-MM-DD-preview for preview versions. Look at examples, descriptions, and any version-related fields.
passCriteria: All api-version values use YYYY-MM-DD format
partialCriteria: Most versions use correct format but some inconsistencies exist

pass.reasoning: Uses correct YYYY-MM-DD format for a GA release.

fail.reasoning: Uses semantic versioning instead of date-based versioning.

rules.title: Support multiple API versions
rules.rationale: APIs should support multiple versions simultaneously to give clients time to migrate. Sudden version deprecation causes client failures.
rules.description: A well-designed API should support at least the current version and one or two previous versions. This allows clients time to update their code when new versions are released.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documentation mentions support for multiple API versions or version deprecation policies.

rules.title: Document version differences
rules.rationale: Clear documentation of version differences helps clients understand what changed and decide when to migrate.

judge.prompt: Check if the API provides documentation about differences between versions or a changelog.

rules.title: Use lowercase paths
rules.rationale: Lowercase paths ensure consistency and avoid case-sensitivity issues across different clients and servers.
rules.description: All URI paths must be lowercase. Mixed case paths can cause confusion and inconsistent behavior across different platforms.

rules.title: Use plural resource names
rules.rationale: Plural resource names indicate collections and maintain consistency with standard REST conventions.
rules.description:
Resource collection names should be plural nouns. Individual resources are accessed by ID within the collection.

For example:
- /users (collection)
- /users/{userId} (individual)

judge.prompt: Check if resource collection paths use plural nouns (users, not user; documents, not document). Individual resources accessed by ID are fine as children of plural collections.
passCriteria: All collection paths use plural nouns
Singleton resources (if any) are clearly documented
partialCriteria: Most paths use plural nouns but some exceptions exist
failCriteria: Collection paths consistently use singular nouns

rules.title: Use kebab-case for multi-word paths
rules.rationale: Kebab-case (hyphen-separated) is the standard for URI path segments and improves readability.

rules.title: Avoid deep nesting
rules.rationale: Deep URL nesting makes APIs harder to use and remember. Most resources can be accessed with 3-4 levels.
rules.description: Paths should not exceed 5-6 segments. If you find yourself needing deeper nesting, consider flattening the structure or using query parameters.

judge.prompt: Check if any paths have more than 6 path segments. Deep nesting makes APIs harder to use and understand.

rules.title: Use camelCase for path parameters
rules.rationale: Path parameter names should use camelCase for consistency with JSON property naming.

rules.title: Use nouns for resources, not verbs
rules.rationale: REST resources should be nouns. The HTTP method conveys the action (GET, POST, etc.).
rules.description: URIs should represent resources (nouns), not actions (verbs). The HTTP method specifies what action to take on the resource.

judge.prompt: Check if URI paths contain action verbs like 'create', 'delete', 'get', 'update', 'list'. These should be expressed through HTTP methods instead.

rules.title: Avoid file extensions in URIs
rules.rationale: Content negotiation should be done via Accept headers, not file extensions.

rules.title: Use consistent resource identifiers
rules.rationale: Resource identifiers should use consistent naming across the API (e.g., always {resourceId} or always {resource-id}).

judge.prompt: Check if resource identifier naming is consistent. For example, if some paths use {userId} and others use {user_id}, that's inconsistent.

rules.title: GET must not have request body
rules.rationale: GET requests must not have a request body per HTTP specification. Request parameters should be in the URL.
rules.description: The HTTP/1.1 specification states that a GET request should not include a message body. Many intermediaries may strip or ignore bodies on GET requests.

rules.title: DELETE should return 204 No Content
rules.rationale: Successful DELETE operations typically have no content to return, so 204 No Content is appropriate.
rules.description: A successful DELETE should return 204 No Content with no response body. If the resource was already deleted, 204 is still appropriate (idempotency).

rules.title: POST should return 201 Created
rules.rationale: POST operations that create resources should return 201 Created with a Location header.
rules.description:
When POST creates a new resource, it should return 201 Created with:
- Location header pointing to the new resource
- The created resource in the response body

rules.title: PUT is for full replacement
rules.rationale: PUT replaces the entire resource. Use PATCH for partial updates.
rules.description:
PUT semantics require sending the complete resource representation. The server replaces the existing resource with the request body.

For partial updates, use PATCH instead.

judge.prompt: Check if PUT operations are documented as full replacement. If PUT is used for partial updates, that's incorrect - PATCH should be used instead.

rules.title: PATCH for partial updates
rules.rationale: PATCH allows clients to send only the fields they want to update, reducing payload size and avoiding conflicts.
rules.description: Use PATCH with application/merge-patch+json for partial resource updates. Only the fields included in the request are modified.

judge.prompt: Check if PATCH operations are available for resources that support updates. PATCH should use merge-patch semantics.

rules.title: HEAD mirrors GET without body
rules.rationale: HEAD should return the same headers as GET but without the response body. Useful for checking resource existence.

judge.prompt: If HEAD operations are defined, verify they return the same headers as the corresponding GET operation.

rules.title: OPTIONS for CORS preflight
rules.rationale: OPTIONS requests are used for CORS preflight. The API should handle them appropriately.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents CORS support or OPTIONS handling for cross-origin requests.

rules.title: Use 200 for successful GET
rules.rationale: Successful GET requests should return 200 OK with the requested resource.

rules.title: Use camelCase for JSON properties
rules.rationale: JSON property names must use camelCase for consistency with JavaScript conventions and other Microsoft APIs.
rules.description: All JSON property names should use camelCase (e.g., firstName, lastName, createdAt). This is consistent with JavaScript naming conventions.

rules.title: Use ISO 8601 for date-time
rules.rationale: ISO 8601 is the international standard for date and time representation and avoids ambiguity.
rules.description: Date-time values must use ISO 8601 format with timezone information (e.g., 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z).

judge.prompt: Check if date and time properties use string type with format 'date-time' (ISO 8601). Look for properties with names like 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'timestamp'.

rules.title: Use strings for resource IDs
rules.rationale: String IDs support various formats including GUIDs, while integers may overflow in JavaScript.
rules.description:
Resource identifiers should be strings rather than integers. This supports:
- GUIDs/UUIDs
- Composite IDs
- Avoidance of JavaScript integer precision issues

judge.prompt: Check if resource ID properties (id, resourceId, etc.) are typed as string rather than integer.

rules.title: Use application/json content type
rules.rationale: JSON is the standard format for Microsoft REST APIs.

rules.title: Support content negotiation
rules.rationale: Accept headers allow clients to specify preferred response formats.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports content negotiation via Accept headers or documents supported media types.

rules.title: Include self link in responses
rules.rationale: Self links help clients discover the canonical URL of a resource.

judge.prompt: Check if resource responses include a self link or @odata.id that points to the resource's canonical URL.

rules.title: Use standard error format
rules.rationale: A consistent error format allows clients to handle errors programmatically and display meaningful messages to users.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses (4xx, 5xx) use the standard Microsoft error format with error.code and error.message fields.
passCriteria: Error format is consistent across all error responses
partialCriteria: Error format is mostly correct but some fields are missing
Error format varies slightly between endpoints
failCriteria: No structured error format is defined
Error responses are plain text or unstructured

migration.summary: Convert error responses to standard Microsoft error format

steps.description: Wrap error in an 'error' envelope object
Add 'code' field with machine-readable error code

rules.title: Include error code
rules.rationale: Machine-readable error codes allow clients to programmatically handle specific error conditions.

judge.prompt: Check if error response schemas include a 'code' property for machine-readable error identification.

rules.title: Include error message
rules.rationale: Human-readable messages help developers understand and debug errors.

judge.prompt: Check if error response schemas include a 'message' property with a human-readable description.

rules.title: Use appropriate HTTP status codes
rules.rationale: HTTP status codes provide a standard way to communicate the result of a request.
rules.description:
Use the most specific HTTP status code for each error condition:
- 400: Bad Request (validation errors)
- 401: Unauthorized (authentication required)
- 403: Forbidden (insufficient permissions)
- 404: Not Found (resource doesn't exist)
- 409: Conflict (resource state conflict)
- 429: Too Many Requests (rate limiting)
- 500: Internal Server Error (unexpected server error)

judge.prompt: Check if the API uses appropriate HTTP status codes for different error conditions. 4xx for client errors, 5xx for server errors.

decisionTables.title: HTTP Status Code Selection
decisionTables.description: Choose the appropriate status code based on the error condition

rules.title: Include error target when applicable
rules.rationale: The target field helps identify which field or parameter caused the error.

judge.prompt: Check if validation error responses include a 'target' field indicating which property caused the error.

rules.title: Support error details for multiple errors
rules.rationale: When multiple errors occur, returning all of them at once saves round trips.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses can include a 'details' array for multiple validation errors.

rules.title: Use nextLink for pagination
rules.rationale: Server-driven pagination with nextLink ensures consistent paging behavior and allows the server to control page size.
rules.description: Collection responses must include a 'nextLink' property when more results are available. The nextLink is an opaque URL that clients should follow without modification.

judge.prompt: Check if collection responses include a 'nextLink' property for pagination. Collections should return {"value": [...], "nextLink": "url"}.
passCriteria: Collection responses use 'value' array for items
nextLink property is present when more results exist
partialCriteria: Pagination exists but uses different property names
nextLink format differs slightly from standard

rules.title: Support $top query parameter
rules.rationale: The $top parameter allows clients to request a specific number of results.

judge.prompt: Check if collection endpoints support $top query parameter to limit the number of results.

rules.title: Support $skip query parameter
rules.rationale: The $skip parameter allows clients to skip a number of results for offset-based pagination.

judge.prompt: Check if collection endpoints support $skip query parameter for offset-based pagination.

rules.title: Support $count query parameter
rules.rationale: The $count parameter allows clients to request the total count of items.

judge.prompt: Check if collection endpoints support $count=true to include total count in the response.

rules.title: Support $filter query parameter
rules.rationale: The $filter parameter enables clients to filter collections server-side, reducing data transfer.
rules.description: Collection endpoints should support $filter for server-side filtering using OData-style expressions.

bad: Requiring client-side filtering of large collections

judge.prompt: Check if collection endpoints support $filter query parameter for server-side filtering.

rules.title: Support $orderby query parameter
rules.rationale: The $orderby parameter enables clients to sort results server-side.

judge.prompt: Check if collection endpoints support $orderby query parameter for sorting.

rules.title: Support $select query parameter
rules.rationale: The $select parameter allows clients to request only specific properties, reducing payload size.

judge.prompt: Check if endpoints support $select query parameter to request specific properties.

rules.title: Support $expand query parameter
rules.rationale: The $expand parameter allows clients to include related resources in a single request.

judge.prompt: Check if endpoints support $expand query parameter to include related resources.

rules.title: Document supported filter operations
rules.rationale: Clients need to know which filter operations are supported for each property.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents which filter operations (eq, ne, gt, lt, contains, etc.) are supported.

rules.title: Use 202 Accepted for long-running operations
rules.rationale: Long-running operations should return immediately with 202 Accepted to avoid HTTP timeouts.
rules.description:
Operations that may take more than a few seconds should:
1. Return 202 Accepted immediately
2. Include a Location header pointing to a status monitor
3. Include Retry-After header with polling interval

judge.prompt: Check if operations that may take a long time return 202 Accepted with a Location header for polling.
passCriteria: Location header is included for status polling
partialCriteria: 202 is used but Location header format differs

rules.title: Include Retry-After header
rules.rationale: Retry-After tells clients when to poll for status, preventing excessive polling.

judge.prompt: Check if 202 Accepted responses include Retry-After header to guide polling frequency.

rules.title: Return operation result on completion
rules.rationale: When an LRO completes, the final status response should include the operation result.

judge.prompt: Check if completed LRO status includes the result or a link to the created resource.

rules.title: Support operation cancellation
rules.rationale: Allowing clients to cancel long-running operations saves resources.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports cancelling long-running operations via DELETE on the operation resource.

rules.title: Use consistent naming patterns
rules.rationale: Consistent naming reduces cognitive load and makes APIs more predictable.
rules.description: Similar concepts should use consistent naming across the API. For example, don't mix 'createdDateTime' and 'createTime'.

judge.prompt: Check for consistent naming patterns. For example, if some schemas use 'createdDateTime' and others use 'createdAt', that's inconsistent.

rules.title: Use full words over abbreviations
rules.rationale: Full words are clearer than abbreviations for API users unfamiliar with domain jargon.

good: identifier (not id, though id is acceptable)

judge.prompt: Check if property names avoid unnecessary abbreviations. 'configuration' is better than 'config'.

rules.title: Use domain-appropriate terminology
rules.rationale: Use terminology that matches the domain and is understood by the target audience.

judge.prompt: Check if the API uses appropriate domain terminology that users would understand.

rules.title: Boolean properties should be positive
rules.rationale: Positive boolean names (isEnabled, isActive) are easier to understand than negative ones.

judge.prompt: Check if boolean property names use positive phrasing (isEnabled) rather than negative (isDisabled).

rules.title: Define security scheme
rules.rationale: APIs must document their authentication requirements for security and usability.
rules.description: Every API must define at least one security scheme in the OpenAPI specification.

rules.title: Apply security globally
rules.rationale: Security should be applied at the API level to ensure all endpoints are protected by default.

rules.title: Use OAuth2 with Azure AD
rules.rationale: OAuth2 with Azure AD provides enterprise-grade authentication and integrates with Microsoft identity.

judge.prompt: Check if the security scheme uses OAuth2 (preferably with Azure AD flows). API key authentication alone is not recommended.

rules.title: Use HTTPS only
rules.rationale: All API traffic must be encrypted using HTTPS to protect sensitive data.

rules.title: Document required scopes
rules.rationale: OAuth scopes define granular permissions; documenting required scopes helps clients request appropriate access.

judge.prompt: Check if OAuth2 scopes are defined and documented for the API operations.

rules.title: Support rate limiting
rules.rationale: Rate limiting protects APIs from abuse and ensures fair resource allocation.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents rate limiting policies or returns 429 Too Many Requests.

rules.title: Return request-id header
rules.rationale: Request IDs enable request tracing and debugging across distributed systems.
rules.description: All responses should include a request-id (or x-ms-request-id) header with a unique identifier for the request.

judge.prompt: Check if responses include a request-id or x-ms-request-id header for request tracing.

rules.title: Support client-request-id header
rules.rationale: Client-provided request IDs help correlate requests with client-side logs.

judge.prompt: Check if the API accepts and echoes client-request-id or x-ms-client-request-id headers.

rules.title: Include Date header
rules.rationale: The Date header indicates when the response was generated.

judge.prompt: Check if responses include the Date header with the response timestamp.

rules.title: Use standard Content-Type header
rules.rationale: Content-Type must accurately describe the response body format.

judge.prompt: Check if responses include appropriate Content-Type headers (application/json for JSON responses).

rules.title: Define all schemas
rules.rationale: All request and response bodies should have defined schemas for documentation and validation.

rules.title: Include schema descriptions
rules.rationale: Schema descriptions help developers understand the purpose of each property.

judge.prompt: Check if schema properties include descriptions explaining their purpose.

rules.title: Use appropriate data types
rules.rationale: Using correct data types enables proper validation and client SDK generation.

judge.prompt: Check if properties use appropriate types: string for text, integer/number for numbers, boolean for true/false, array for lists.

rules.title: Define required properties
rules.rationale: Marking required properties helps clients understand what data must be provided.

judge.prompt: Check if schemas define which properties are required vs optional.

rules.title: Use enums for fixed values
rules.rationale: Enums document valid values and enable validation.

judge.prompt: Check if properties with a fixed set of allowed values use enum definitions.

rules.title: Include format for strings
rules.rationale: String formats (date-time, email, uri) enable proper validation and documentation.

judge.prompt: Check if string properties include format specifiers (date-time, email, uri, uuid) where appropriate.

rules.title: Use value array for collections
rules.rationale: Microsoft APIs use 'value' as the property name for collection arrays to ensure consistency.
rules.description: Collection responses must use a 'value' property to contain the array of items.

judge.prompt: Check if collection responses use 'value' as the property name for the items array.

rules.title: Include @odata.count when requested
rules.rationale: Total count helps clients display pagination information.

judge.prompt: Check if collection responses include @odata.count or count property when $count=true is requested.

rules.title: Return empty array for empty collections
rules.rationale: Empty collections should return an empty array, not null or omit the property.

judge.prompt: Check if collection responses return an empty array [] when no items match, not null.

rules.title: Support ETag for resources
rules.rationale: ETags enable optimistic concurrency control and efficient caching.
rules.description: Resources that support updates should return an ETag header. The ETag value should change whenever the resource changes.

judge.prompt: Check if GET responses include ETag headers for resources that can be updated.

rules.title: Support If-Match for updates
rules.rationale: If-Match prevents lost updates by requiring clients to provide the current ETag.
rules.description: PUT and PATCH operations should support If-Match header to prevent concurrent modification conflicts.

judge.prompt: Check if PUT/PATCH operations document support for If-Match header with ETag values.

rules.title: Return 412 for ETag mismatch
rules.rationale: 412 Precondition Failed indicates the resource was modified since the client last fetched it.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents 412 Precondition Failed response for ETag mismatches.

rules.title: Support If-None-Match for caching
rules.rationale: If-None-Match enables efficient caching by returning 304 Not Modified when resources haven't changed.

judge.prompt: Check if GET operations support If-None-Match header for cache validation.

rules.title: Avoid breaking changes
rules.rationale: Breaking changes force clients to update their code and can cause outages.
rules.description:
API changes within a version must be backward compatible:
- Don't remove fields from responses
- Don't change field types
- Don't add required fields to request bodies
- Don't change the meaning of existing fields

judge.prompt: Check if the API design avoids patterns that typically lead to breaking changes.

rules.title: New fields should be optional
rules.rationale: Adding required fields to existing requests breaks existing clients.

judge.prompt: Check if new request body fields are marked as optional to maintain backward compatibility.

rules.title: Use extensible enums
rules.rationale: Enums should be designed to allow new values without breaking clients.
rules.description: Clients should handle unknown enum values gracefully. The x-ms-enum extension with modelAsString can help.

judge.prompt: Check if the API uses extensible enum patterns that allow adding new values without breaking clients.

rules.title: Document deprecations clearly
rules.rationale: Clear deprecation notices give clients time to migrate.

judge.prompt: Check if deprecated features are marked with OpenAPI deprecated: true and include migration guidance.

rules.title: Support distributed tracing headers
rules.rationale: Distributed tracing enables end-to-end request tracking across services.
rules.description: APIs should support and propagate traceparent and tracestate headers (W3C Trace Context) for distributed tracing.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents support for traceparent or correlation ID headers.

rules.title: Include correlation-id in responses
rules.rationale: Correlation IDs help track requests across distributed systems for debugging.
rules.description: Responses should include x-ms-correlation-request-id or similar correlation header that links requests.

judge.prompt: Check if responses include correlation headers for request tracking.

rules.title: Support idempotency for POST operations
rules.rationale: Idempotent POST operations prevent duplicate resource creation during retries.
rules.description: POST operations should support idempotency via client-provided request IDs or natural keys. Use Repeatability-Request-ID header for retries.

judge.prompt: Check if POST operations support idempotency through request IDs or natural keys.

rules.title: Support Repeatability-Request-ID header
rules.rationale: Repeatability headers enable safe retries without duplicate side effects.
rules.description: Support Repeatability-Request-ID and Repeatability-First-Sent headers for retry scenarios. Return same result for repeated requests.

judge.prompt: Check if the API documents support for repeatability headers.

rules.title: Document field mutability
rules.rationale: Knowing whether fields can be updated helps clients understand API behavior.
rules.description: Document whether each property is: write-once (only set on create), read-only (server-generated), or read-write (can be updated).

judge.prompt: Check if schema properties document their mutability (read-only, write-once, read-write).

rules.title: Use readOnly for computed properties
rules.rationale: Marking computed properties as readOnly prevents clients from trying to set them.
rules.description: Properties that are server-generated (id, createdAt, etag) should be marked readOnly: true in the schema.

judge.prompt: Check if server-generated properties like id, createdAt are marked as readOnly.

rules.title: Return Deprecation header for deprecated APIs
rules.rationale: Deprecation header alerts clients programmatically about deprecated endpoints.
rules.description: Deprecated API versions or endpoints should return Deprecation header with deprecation date.

judge.prompt: Check if deprecated endpoints return Deprecation header.

rules.title: Include Sunset header for deprecated APIs
rules.rationale: Sunset header tells clients when an API will be permanently removed.
rules.description: APIs scheduled for removal should include Sunset header with the removal date.

judge.prompt: Check if APIs scheduled for removal include Sunset header.

rules.title: Support batch operations
rules.rationale: Batch operations reduce round trips for bulk operations.
rules.description: For high-volume scenarios, support JSON batch requests to process multiple operations in a single HTTP request.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports batch operations for bulk processing.

rules.title: Return 207 Multi-Status for batch results
rules.rationale: 207 Multi-Status allows returning different status codes for each operation in a batch.
rules.description: Batch operations should return 207 Multi-Status with individual status codes for each operation.

judge.prompt: Check if batch operations return 207 Multi-Status with per-operation results.

rules.title: Use POST for action operations
rules.rationale: Non-CRUD actions on resources should use POST with a clear action name.
rules.description: For operations that don't fit CRUD semantics (e.g., start, stop, cancel), use POST to a sub-resource named after the action.

judge.prompt: Check if non-CRUD actions use POST with action name in path (e.g., :cancel or /cancel).

rules.title: Use colon notation for actions
rules.rationale: Colon notation clearly distinguishes actions from resources.
rules.description: Actions on resources should use colon notation: /resources/{id}:actionName. This pattern is used in Azure APIs.

judge.prompt: Check if action endpoints use colon notation (:actionName) for clarity.

rules.title: Return Location header on resource creation
rules.rationale: Location header provides the URL of the newly created resource.
rules.description: 201 Created responses must include Location header pointing to the created resource.

judge.prompt: Check if 201 Created responses include Location header with resource URL.

rules.title: Use Azure-AsyncOperation for LRO polling
rules.rationale: Azure-AsyncOperation header provides the operation status URL.
rules.description: Azure LROs should return Azure-AsyncOperation header in addition to Location for status polling.

judge.prompt: Check if LRO responses include Azure-AsyncOperation or Operation-Location header.

rules.title: Include operation status in LRO response
rules.rationale: Operation status indicates whether the operation is still running, succeeded, or failed.
rules.description: LRO status responses must include a status field with values: NotStarted, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled.

judge.prompt: Check if LRO status responses include a status field with standard values.

rules.title: Include error in failed LRO
rules.rationale: Failed operations must include error information for troubleshooting.
rules.description: When an LRO fails, the status response must include error object with code and message.

judge.prompt: Check if failed LRO responses include error object with code and message.

rules.title: Support maxpagesize parameter
rules.rationale: Clients can request a specific page size up to the server's maximum.
rules.description: Support maxpagesize query parameter or Prefer: maxpagesize=N header to control page size.

judge.prompt: Check if collection endpoints support maxpagesize parameter.

rules.title: Support delta queries
rules.rationale: Delta queries enable efficient synchronization by returning only changes.
rules.description: For frequently accessed collections, support delta queries that return changes since the last request via deltaLink.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports delta queries for incremental synchronization.

rules.title: Support upsert with PUT
rules.rationale: Upsert simplifies client logic by creating or updating in one operation.
rules.description: PUT operations may support upsert semantics: create if not exists, update if exists.

judge.prompt: Check if PUT operations support upsert semantics.

rules.title: DELETE should be idempotent
rules.rationale: Deleting an already-deleted resource should succeed, not return 404.
rules.description: DELETE operations must be idempotent. Deleting a non-existent resource should return 204, not 404.

judge.prompt: Check if DELETE operations are documented as idempotent (no error on re-delete).

rules.title: Document soft delete behavior
rules.rationale: Soft delete allows resource recovery and meets compliance requirements.
rules.description: If soft delete is supported, document the retention period and recovery mechanism.

judge.prompt: Check if soft delete behavior is documented when applicable.

rules.title: Document null handling
rules.rationale: Clear null semantics prevent confusion about missing vs null values.
rules.description: Document whether null values are allowed and their meaning (unset vs default).

judge.prompt: Check if null handling semantics are documented for nullable properties.

rules.title: Use null to clear optional fields
rules.rationale: Consistent semantics for clearing field values via PATCH.
rules.description: In PATCH requests, sending null for an optional field should clear/reset it.

judge.prompt: Check if PATCH operations document how to clear optional fields.

rules.title: Support webhook subscriptions
rules.rationale: Webhooks enable real-time notifications without polling.
rules.description: For event-driven scenarios, support webhook subscriptions with subscription management endpoints.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports webhook subscriptions for event notifications.

rules.title: Include validation challenge for webhooks
rules.rationale: Validation challenges verify webhook endpoint ownership.
rules.description: Webhook creation should include a validation challenge that the endpoint must echo back.

judge.prompt: Check if webhook subscriptions include validation challenge mechanism.

rules.title: Include Cache-Control headers
rules.rationale: Cache-Control enables efficient caching and reduces server load.
rules.description: GET responses should include appropriate Cache-Control headers (no-cache, max-age, etc.).

judge.prompt: Check if GET responses include Cache-Control headers.

rules.title: Support conditional GET with Last-Modified
rules.rationale: Last-Modified enables time-based conditional requests.
rules.description: Support Last-Modified response header and If-Modified-Since request header for caching.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports Last-Modified and If-Modified-Since headers.

rules.title: Support $search query parameter
rules.rationale: Free-text search enables users to find resources without knowing exact field values.
rules.description: Support $search query parameter for full-text search across multiple properties.

judge.prompt: Check if collections support $search for full-text search.

rules.title: Use discriminator for polymorphic types
rules.rationale: Discriminators enable proper deserialization of polymorphic types.
rules.description: Polymorphic schemas using oneOf/anyOf should include a discriminator property (e.g., @odata.type).

judge.prompt: Check if polymorphic schemas use discriminator for type identification.

rules.title: Use @odata.type for derived types
rules.rationale: OData type annotations enable runtime type identification.
rules.description: For APIs using OData conventions, include @odata.type for polymorphic resources.

judge.prompt: Check if polymorphic resources include @odata.type annotation.

rules.title: Include resource links
rules.rationale: Resource links enable navigation without URL construction.
rules.description: Resources should include links to related resources or actions (self, parent, children).

judge.prompt: Check if resources include navigation links to related resources.

rules.title: Use @odata.id for resource identity
rules.rationale: OData ID provides canonical resource URL.
rules.description: For OData-style APIs, include @odata.id with the canonical URL of the resource.

judge.prompt: Check if resources include @odata.id or self link.

rules.title: Use UTC for all timestamps
rules.rationale: UTC timestamps avoid timezone confusion and simplify comparison.
rules.description: All date-time values should be in UTC with 'Z' suffix. Avoid local time zones.

judge.prompt: Check if timestamps use UTC with Z suffix.

rules.title: Support time zone in date-only contexts
rules.rationale: Date-only values may need timezone context for interpretation.
rules.description: When using date (without time), document whether it's interpreted in UTC or a specific timezone.

judge.prompt: Check if date-only fields document timezone interpretation.

rules.title: Support Accept-Language for localization
rules.rationale: Accept-Language enables localized responses for user-facing content.
rules.description: Support Accept-Language header for localizing error messages and display content.

judge.prompt: Check if the API supports Accept-Language for localized content.

rules.title: Support region parameter for data residency
rules.rationale: Region parameters support data residency and sovereignty requirements.
rules.description: For multi-region APIs, include region in the URL path or use region-specific hostnames.

judge.prompt: Check if multi-region APIs include region parameter or region-specific endpoints.

rules.title: Include Azure subscription context
rules.rationale: Azure APIs require subscription and resource group context for resource management.
rules.description: Azure Resource Manager APIs must include /subscriptions/{subscriptionId} and optionally /resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName} in the path.

judge.prompt: Check if Azure ARM APIs include proper subscription and resource group path segments.

rules.title: Use provider namespace in Azure paths
rules.rationale: Provider namespaces identify the resource provider responsible for the resource type.
rules.description: Azure ARM paths must include /providers/{provider-namespace}/{resource-type} pattern.

judge.prompt: Check if Azure ARM APIs use proper provider namespace pattern.

rules.title: Support multi-tenant isolation
rules.rationale: Multi-tenant APIs must ensure tenant isolation for security.
rules.description: Multi-tenant APIs must include tenant context in path or via headers and enforce tenant isolation.

judge.prompt: Check if multi-tenant APIs include tenant context and isolation.

rules.title: Minimize PII in URLs
rules.rationale: PII in URLs can be logged and exposed, violating privacy requirements.
rules.description: Avoid including personal identifiable information (email, names) in URL paths or query parameters.

judge.prompt: Check if URLs avoid including PII like email addresses or names.

rules.title: Include operation descriptions
rules.rationale: Operation descriptions help developers understand API behavior.
rules.description: Every operation should have a description explaining its purpose and behavior.

rules.title: Include operation summary
rules.rationale: Operation summaries provide quick understanding of endpoint purpose.
rules.description: Every operation should have a summary (short title) in addition to description.

rules.title: Include example values
rules.rationale: Examples help developers understand expected data formats.
rules.description: Schema properties should include example values to illustrate expected formats.

judge.prompt: Check if schemas include example values for important properties.

rules.title: Document validation constraints
rules.rationale: Validation constraints help clients submit valid requests.
rules.description: Document validation constraints: minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, etc.

judge.prompt: Check if schemas include validation constraints for user-submitted fields.

rules.title: Return Retry-After for 429 responses
rules.rationale: Retry-After helps clients implement proper backoff for rate limiting.
rules.description: 429 Too Many Requests responses must include Retry-After header with seconds to wait.

judge.prompt: Check if 429 responses include Retry-After header.

rules.title: Return Retry-After for 503 responses
rules.rationale: Retry-After helps clients handle temporary service unavailability.
rules.description: 503 Service Unavailable responses should include Retry-After header.

judge.prompt: Check if 503 responses include Retry-After header.

rules.title: Support inner error for debugging
rules.rationale: Inner error provides additional debugging context without exposing to end users.
rules.description: Error responses may include innererror object with additional technical details for debugging.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses support innererror for additional debugging context.
